paper_metadata.title: Experimental implementation of quantum-walk-based portfolio optimization

summary: The paper experimentally implements the Quantum Walk‑based Optimization Algorithm (QWOA) operators using a single‑photon linear‑optical network encoding a 7‑dimensional qudit representing the 7 valid portfolios of a 3‑asset Markowitz problem. For circuit depths p=1–6, the probability of the optimal portfolio state increases experimentally from 0.324 to 0.797 (theory up to ≈0.998), demonstrating probability amplification consistent with the QWOA model.

experiments.description: Experimental implementation of the quantum-walk-based portfolio optimization (QWOA) mixing and phase-shift unitaries for a 3-asset portfolio using single-photon linear optics, evaluated for circuit depths p=1 to 6.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Walk-based Optimization Algorithm (QWOA) for portfolio optimization; restricted experimental implementation of phase-shift and continuous-time quantum walk unitaries
algorithm.ansatz: Alternating phase-shift unitary U_Q'(γ) and indexed-walk unitary U_w'(t)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not reported; parameters optimized separately for each p
algorithm.parameter_initialization: uniform distribution between 0 and 2π for 20 repeats at each p

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: γ and t initialized from [0, 2π] for optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits per asset encode three positions: |10⟩ short, |01⟩ long, |00⟩ or |11⟩ no position; for 3 assets this gives a 6-qubit full encoding, but the experiment restricts to the 7 valid solutions under constraint a=0 and implements them as a 7-dimensional qudit basis.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Mean-variance Markowitz cost C(s)=ω Σ_{i,j=1}^M σ_{ij} z_i z_j − (1−ω) Σ_{i=1}^M r_i z_i, with constraint a=Σ_i z_i=0
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraint a=0 handled by restricting to the valid solution subspace S' of 7 portfolios; invalid states excluded by classical indexing/preparation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal quality operator Q=diag(q0,...,q6) over the valid-solution subspace; QWOA uses U_Q'(γ)=e^{-iγQ} and U_w'(t)=e^{-iWt} on K7

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization for three stocks under a net-zero position constraint

dataset_specification.description: Google, IBM, Microsoft; date range 2019-01-01 to 2020-12-31; adjusted closing prices used to compute returns and covariance

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Expected returns and covariance matrix computed from daily closing/opening prices; quality values q_i calculated classically from adjusted closing prices; q values scaled by factor 250 for optimization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Experimental and theoretical probability distributions compared for p=1 to 6; expectation value of quality operator measured; photon counts recorded for 10 s per setting with approximately 27,000 single photons registered

noise_model.noise_type: interferometer imperfections and wave-plate inaccuracies; dephasing estimated at ~0.97

implementation_details.classical_solver: BFGS for parameter optimization; QuOp_MPI used for simulation/parameter search
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of valid solutions, indexing, returns, covariance matrix, and optimal variational parameters
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Projective measurement via PBS; probabilities estimated from photon-count ratios; expectation value of Q computed from measured distributions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: objective value decreases with p; probability of optimal state increases and stabilizes

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical portfolio optimization / prior QAOA-based methods
speedup_claims.conditions: as stated for QWOA in cited prior work; not experimentally benchmarked here
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity statement from prior work, not a measured speedup in this experiment.

speedup_claims.factor: reduced search space from 64 to 7 states
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a problem-restriction advantage, not a runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(m^2) gate complexity for QWOA as stated in the paper (from cited prior work)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiment restricted to a 7‑state solution subspace representing a 3‑asset portfolio.
limiting_factors: Toy problem size (3 assets, 7 valid portfolios)
No classical baseline comparison in experiment
Optical implementation realizes only restricted subspace unitaries rather than full scalable circuit
Variational parameters optimized classically and precomputed via simulation
Scaling of optical interferometer network not demonstrated

notes: The experiment is photonic and gate-based (single photons, linear optics), not quantum annealing.
The paper explicitly states p=1 to 6 and gives the implemented unitaries U1...U6; circuit_depth recorded as 6 iterations.

num_qubits=7 is inferred from the 7-dimensional qudit implementation and the seven basis states; the paper also notes the full 3-asset encoding would be 6 qubits, but the experiment uses a 7-state restricted subspace.
The paper does not claim a demonstrated quantum advantage; it presents a proof‑of‑principle optical realization of QWOA operators.
Results only show agreement between experimental and theoretical probability amplification for a small 3‑asset portfolio instance.
